KEY006 / KEY007 - Same Composer
works.notes:
This one is particularly difficult because the Original Publisher has two different Sub-Publishers in one territory, and that same Original Publisher has two other different Sub-Publishers in another territory. On Curve, you just find this Original Publisher four times, which in CWR needs to be translated with the same Original Publisher having two SPU lines. The tricky part is to make sure the two correct Sub-Publishers are following the correct SPU of the Original Publisher, and for these not to be swapped around.

In this scenario, you need to thus look at the combination of the Original Publisher and Composers, to know which pair to match the right Sub-Publisher to in the CWR format.

Also in DP1, John Smith doesn't need SWTs to include and then exclude a territory again.

works.title: Two different Original Publishers with same Sub-Publisher in one territory and different Sub-Publishers in another territory.
Two different Sub-Publishers in one Territory, one Sub-Publisher in another
works.notes:
This is a tricky one. Usually, an Original Publisher has just one SPU. But we found that in the case where an Original Publisher has two different sub-publishers in the same territory, that you need two SPUs for that same Original Publisher. In this case we have both scenarios in two territories, so what do you do when creating a CWR for both?

If we want to be consistent, I believe you'd need to have the two SPUs, because there's no other option for Belgium. That would mean that you also need to split the collected share of the Sub-Publisher in World Ex BE across the two SPUs. We essentially need to make a calculation to see how this collected share is split across the two SPUs. I'd do it in proportion of the Owned Shares across the two SPUs.

However, as per CWR rules, I don't think what we currently do is incorrect. We do list just one SPU for the Original Publisher, and list all Sub-Publishers. The total owned and collected shares are correct. I'd just keep things this way, until we have a society telling us otherwise.

works.title: Writer is both Controlled and Uncontrolled in same Territory
Writer with 0 collected share
works.notes:
CWR documentation says that you can't have an SWT where all collected shares are zero. This makes me think (though is not confirmed in the documentation) that if we have a writer without a collected share that we need to simply not have an SWT. Interestingly, we found Maestro exports it with an SWT with 0% collected shares. Abby North also confirmed that ASCAP accepts this. (From SESAC: This file passes our technical validations (thus, won't get rejected) but does not log a performance share for the translator (since there's no territory line included, our system interprets that there being no USA claim valid for that SWR). I'm sure different societies may have different interpretations of that setup but your former test would be more accurate for us.)

So whilst technically incorrect, societies prefer it this way, so we'll consider this one to be correct.
